text:
Diego Morales: Hi all 84 I'm a new hire (started 06/24) and have a couple onboarding questions about benefits and a tuition reimbursement form. 1) Is the 30-day window for making benefit elections from my start date or the end of the orientation week? 2) If I miss the window, can it be treated as a qualifying life event? 3) I uploaded the tuition pre-approval form but haven't seen confirmation. 4) Also curious when 401(k) employer match kicks in for new hires — first paycheck or after 30 days?

Ava (People Ops): Welcome Diego! Short answers: 1) Elections window is 30 days from your hire date (HR policy). 2) Missing it is not automatically a QLE; you need a qualifying event to enroll mid-year. 3) Tuition pre-approval goes to Total Rewards for sign-off (Rina queues it). 4) Employer match eligibility depends on plan rules; often there's a 30-day waiting period but contributions start when you enroll. Rina can confirm plan specifics and Sanya can check your tuition upload.

Diego Morales: Thanks Ava. I uploaded the tuition form to Bamboo on 06/25 as "Diego_tuition_preapproval_062524.pdf" and cc'd my manager. No reply yet. Would prefer the reimbursement to cover a July class that starts 07/02. Any way to expedite?

Rina (Total Rewards): Hey Diego, saw your upload. We route pre-approval to manager + Total Rewards. If your manager already approved in the portal, I can fast-track. Can you DM me the manager approval screenshot or confirm manager name so I can check?

Diego Morales: Manager is Kira Patel — she approved via the portal and I also have an email thread. DMing screenshot now.

OnboardBot: Document "Diego_tuition_preapproval_062524.pdf" linked to ticket TR-9981.

Rina (Total Rewards): Got it  thanks. I marked TR-9981 for expedited review since class starts 07/02. We usually need proof of enrollment + course syllabus. If those are missing, we can provisionally approve and hold final payment until receipt of syllabus. Expect a decision by 06/28.

Diego Morales: Appreciate it. Back to benefits window: if I make zero elections by 07/24 (30 days), will I be defaulted into anything? Specifically worried about HSA vs non-HSA medical plans.

Sanya (Benefits): If you make no election by the deadline, you default to "waive" for voluntary benefits and the system may assign the base medical plan as "employee only" for carrier purposes depending on payroll import. HSAs require active enrollment; you won't be enrolled automatically. If you think you'll want HSA, enroll before 07/24. If you miss it, enrollment typically waits until annual open enrollment unless a QLE occurs.

Diego Morales: Good to know. Hypothetical Q: My spouse was on a company plan previously and lost coverage on 06/15. If I enroll and add them, is that a QLE that would let me enroll outside the window?

Sanya (Benefits): Yes, loss of other employer coverage is a QLE. You'd need documentation showing the spouse's coverage end date. QLE effective date rules vary by carrier but usually allow enrollment retro to the date of loss or the date you enroll within the QLE window (30 days). Upload the proof and tag benefits@redwood.com.

Diego Morales: OK I'll keep that in mind. About 401(k) match: I enrolled in the 401(k) on 06/26 through the retirement portal and set 6% deferral. When does employer match hit my payroll? First paycheck after enrollment or after a vesting period?

Liam (Payroll): Employer match contributions are made on each payroll period once the employee is actively enrolled. There may be a plan-specific eligibility (e.g., 30 days or first of month) and vesting schedule determines ownership over time. Our plan makes the match for the pay period once enrollment is effective; vesting is separate (check the SPD). I can check your specific eligibility if you DM me your employee ID.

Diego Morales: DM sent. Also saw a line item on my preview paystub labeled "FICA Additional Withholding?" Should I box that as something to discuss with payroll?

Liam (Payroll): Thanks Diego. I checked your record: the FICA Additional line is for supplemental tax withholding elections you can use for taxable reimbursements. It's not a default line; I think that was left on from a test record and we removed it. It shouldn't appear on final paystubs. If it does on 07/01, DM me and I'll correct the feed.

Diego Morales: Last tiny Q 6 holiday policy: I started mid-year; do company-paid holidays accrue or are they pro-rated for new hires? For example, we have a floating day policy and a regional holiday coming up 07/04.

Ava (People Ops): Company holidays are not prorated; if you are an active employee on the holiday date you receive the day. Floating days are granted at hire and are subject to blackout rules for certain teams; check your manager if you plan to use a floating day close to a start date.

Diego Morales: Fantastic. Thanks everyone for the help and speed. Will follow up if anything still pending. :raised_hands:
